title: Network Access Boundary
problem: Self-hosted Taru needs explicit remote access policy, trusted proxy/header behavior, tunnel-provider readiness, origin constraints, and redacted diagnostics before built-in NAT traversal or broader remote-client features are safe.
gates: npm run check from apps/admin-web after Admin contract/client changes

continue_policy.notes: NAB-010 opened Network Access Boundary as the next post-DWI mainline lane. NAB-020 completed network access policy/config validation for local-only, reverse-proxy, private-network, and tunnel-provider modes with trusted proxy source requirements, origin validation, tunnel token-env checks, deployment docs, and no tunnel runtime. NAB-030 completed request-time HTTP boundary enforcement for configured browser origins, CORS preflight, auth-order preservation, public health compatibility, and trusted forwarded host/proto handling gated by exact-IP/CIDR trusted proxy sources. NAB-040 completed Admin-only network readiness diagnostics in system config plus generated Admin Web contract/data mapping with strict redaction and no Public Client protocol churn. Continue with NAB-050 closeout/follow-on split. Do not add built-in NAT traversal runtime, relay services, identity/RBAC, protocol downloaders, AI writes, Addon runtime/distribution, direct library writes, Public Client API changes, or taru-client-protocol changes unless split into a dedicated lane.
